full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 1 to 10 to show cause as to why section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Annexure-G) shall not be declared void and ultra vires and as to why Order No. 9 dated 10-5-2004 (Annexure-F) dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2004 filed by the petitioners passed by the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2004 rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect." 

 3. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the petitioners as 3rd party in the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 89 of 2003 having knowledge of the auction sale of the suit property on 26-4-2004 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2004 against order of the Auction Sale of the suit property which was rejected by order impugned against dated 10-5-2004 (in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2004). The application of the petitioners was rejected as Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2004 and the Adalat ordered to deposit 25% of the decretal amount (as the law then was) under section 32(2) of the Ain. But the petitioners did not deposit the same as a result the Miscellaneous Case was rejected by the Adalat for non-deposition of the legal amount under law (Annexure-F). 

 5. Mr Md Kamruzzaman, the learned counsel for the respondent-bank, on the other hand by filing affidavit-in-opposition opposes the Rule. In paragraph 15 he has stated that in compliance of the provision of sections 32(2) and 33(3) the respondent-bank published the auction notice. It came in the Daily Newspapers fixing 10-5-2004 for date of auction sale of the mortgaged property for recovery of outstanding dues in the Money Execution Case No.89 of 2003. Therefore, the learned counsel for the respondent-bank assertively submits that deposit of 25% of the decretal amount is condition precedent for making an application by any 3rd party in any proceeding of Artha Jari Case. There is no escape from this provision which is a mandatory one. He further submits that section 26 of the Ain is not in conflict with section 32(2) of the Ain in any manner. It could be found from the petition that section 32(2) of the Ain has been offending the provision of section 26 of the same. 

 6. That being the position the question that needs to be addressed in this petition whether the provision of section 32(2) under the facts and circumstances of the present case is unconstitutional and consequently the order impugned against has been passed without any lawful authority having no legal effect. 

 9. Therefore, on a plain reading of the said section we find that the procedure of money execution proceeding as laid down in Code of Civil Procedure shall equally apply in case of provision of Ain (execution). On the other hand, section 32(1)(2) is a positive special law under the Ain. In clear terms the law postulates: 

 10. The law itself is absolutely clear without any ambiguity. It has made provision for deposition of 25% of the decretal amount where any 3rd party wants to join in execution proceeding to ventilate grievances. Since the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is special law it will override any other law if there is no inconsistency in the special law itself. As we remarked already that there is no conflict or inconsistency in respect of the relevant law so to say in any manner even with the Code of Civil Procedure far less to talk about any other law. Then how can it be thought that this provision of special law has infringed or has been passed in violation of any fundamental right as enshrined in the Constitution we do not understand. There is no dearth of law in our armoury but often we come across that on a flimsy ground as it has happened in the present case effort being made by bringing some un-call for arguments to establish a case on the ground of violation of fundamental rights of the Constitution. Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special law making a special provision for recovery of outstanding dues of the financial institution which we have already mentioned. We hold that none of the laws  under the Artha Rin Ain is in conflict with any  of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution. 

 11. Section 32(2) is a positive law that mandates deposit of 25% (as the law then was) of the decreetal amount for filing a miscellaneous case. The petitioner without depositing the same filed miscellaneous case and the Adalat in absolute keeping with the provision rejected the miscellaneous case which is immuned from interference by this Division.
